<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `requiredPermissions (literal, 42 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e69fa46dd326c4dcbbce206f35c8b3398776e76e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2c2bc8501344021b437d42b11ee78a0c6e7a4264` — the merge of head `7ef98ab887129f0f0a27f06e359fd8a0f3cbb986` into base `e69fa46dd326c4dcbbce206f35c8b3398776e76e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2c2bc8501344021b437d42b11ee78a0c6e7a4264 && git checkout 2c2bc8501344021b437d42b11ee78a0c6e7a4264
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e69fa46dd326c4dcbbce206f35c8b3398776e76e 7ef98ab887129f0f0a27f06e359fd8a0f3cbb986 && git checkout -B drift-repro e69fa46dd326c4dcbbce206f35c8b3398776e76e && git merge --no-ff 7ef98ab887129f0f0a27f06e359fd8a0f3cbb986

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e69fa46dd326c4dcbbce206f35c8b3398776e76e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bd91d5c0fa9cdc24e271f4f763550ac3a37524d3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.form.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.form.ts + packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/metadata-form-zh-cn.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/metadata-form-i18n.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-view-audience-save-round-trip.test.ts
Security-touching: yes
Rule-change-verified: none

Inputs read: card #34908 (body and all five comments: triage 6953426292, split 7016189680, analysis 7098042572, ruling 7103739693, claim 7210714615), PR #37839 (body, 26-file list, net diff against `main`; the merge base is `main` at 1028438748d, so the head carries no stale base), and the check-runs on the head. No earlier `## Contract review` record exists on the card or the PR.

Check-runs on this head at the time of reading: 11 completed `success` (Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, Spec property liveness, filter), 10 `skipped` (opt-in and schedule jobs), none failed. STILL PENDING, so not judged here: Build Core, Build UI Deps, Test Core 1/10 to 10/10, Live E2E UI, Type Check (consumer gates, debt ledger, source gates, workspace), and all eight Lint jobs (CI/release/engine gates, ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, docs and code guards, repo and tooling gates, and the three scoped ones). This record's reading of the tree does not stand in for those conclusions; the queue waits for them.

### ① Derived judgments

- `viewForm` gains one row, `requiredPermissions` (`string-tags`), in `navigation_sharing`. RIGHT. The key is declared on the list-view shape (`view.zod.ts:3786`, `z.array(z.string()).optional()`), its liveness row is `live` (`liveness/view.json:175-180`), and the widget is the one the ruling's execution names ("same widget as `app.form.ts:102`").
- `dashboardForm` gains a collapsed `Access` section holding the same row. RIGHT. `DashboardSchema.requiredPermissions` is declared at the root (`dashboard.zod.ts:1888`); the dashboard form has no `navigation_sharing` section, so a section of its own is the only place the ruled "matching row" can sit. It mirrors `app.form.ts:98-102`.
- No schema key, accepted value, gate or export changes. RIGHT, verified on the diff: no `*.zod.ts`, no `meta-item-read-gate.ts`, no barrel touched.
- The two `omit` ledger entries (`view` and `dashboard` root `requiredPermissions`) are dropped from `metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts`. RIGHT. Their stated reason was "declared, not enforced yet ... whether to offer it then is a ruling for the enforcement"; the gate is live (#22639) and ruling 7103739693 is that ruling. Leaving them would have failed the ledger's own non-vacuity rule once the form offers the key.
- The generated `metadataForms` bundles and source hashes (ten locales), the 840 to 843 positive control, and the two console zh-CN overlays follow from the three new leaves (two row labels, one section label). RIGHT as a derivation; their content is the lane seat's ACCEPT, except the two overlay files, read in ④.
- Where the row writes: Studio's `ViewVariantInspector.tsx:569-579` hands `viewForm` the variant body and writes the whole body back under the variant key, so the key lands in the list body (`config.requiredPermissions` on a view item), which is one of the two positions `filterViewForUser` asks (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:963-965`). The row writes where the gate reads. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/34908-view-dashboard-audience-form-row.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in both the changeset body and the PR body. This matches what the diff publishes: nothing a metadata author can write changes (no key, value or type), so the kind is `none` and `none` takes `patch` (AGENTS.md, "Add a changeset for anything that publishes"). The three packages named are the three released packages the diff moves. `Check Changeset` concluded `success`. Correct.

Nit (changeset prose, not reviewed further): the body says "zh-CN reads ... the other locales fall back to the English source", while the tree also carries authored ja-JP and es-ES leaves.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag 1 (PR "Acceptance notes"): the ruling names `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectListViewInspector.tsx`, which is not on `main`. ANSWERED: confirmed absent on `main`; Studio's view panel is `metadata-admin/inspectors/ViewVariantInspector.tsx`, which renders `viewForm` through `SchemaForm`, so the row appears there with no UI change. The picker belongs to the ruled second PR against that file. No scope change, no escalation.
- Dev flag 2: seven locales (ar, de, fr, ko, pt-BR, ru, zh-Hant) carry the English source for the three new leaves. ANSWERED: extractor fills with source hashes, the standing practice for form rows; the lane seat's ACCEPT, not a contract question.
- Third-tier premise (b) of the ruling's execution, with its fork rule: the save door must keep `requiredPermissions`. ANSWERED by `meta-view-audience-save-round-trip.test.ts`: the console envelope (gate under `config`), drafted with `If-None-Match: *` and published through the real routes over better-sqlite3, keeps the key in the draft read, the stored active row and the served item; a holder is served and a non-holder is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`; clearing stores no key. No fork. Its run conclusion is among the pending Test Core shards.
- `open_questions`: none declared on the PR or the claim.
- NOT MEASURED by the dev: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (left to CI). The corresponding Build Core job is pending on this head.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to find.
- Security-touching reads `yes`: the changed hunks teach permission behaviour (who is served a view or a dashboard). No `hits` path is under `skills/**`, so the skills arm does not apply; the adopting seat decides the `security` label.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ui/view.form.ts` and `packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.form.ts`, against ruling 7103739693 (letter B), the execution in 7098042572 step 1, the describe they restate (`audience-required-permissions.ts`), the gate they describe (`meta-item-read-gate.ts`) and their first consumers (`ViewVariantInspector.tsx`, `dashboard-schema.ts#getDashboardForm` feeding `DashboardDefaultInspector.tsx` and the in-page dashboard editor).

What holds:
- Ruled shape: the existing key, an authoring row, no second audience key, no any-of form, the `string-tags` face. Both files do exactly that.
- Each hint clause against the describe and the gate: "every one listed" is `holdsRequiredPermissions` (`every`, `:843`); "leave it empty" is the absent-or-empty arm; "one capability granted to each group's permission set" is clause 2 of the describe; "a position passes on the ones its permission sets grant" is `position.zod.ts` (capability only through permission sets); "does not find it in the list and is refused if they open it directly" is the list gate and the by-name `403`. No clause contradicts the code.
- The dashboard hints stay inside the #36816 vocabulary rule (`DEVELOPER_VOCABULARY` matches nothing in the new text).
- The form-only direction is safe: both keys are live, non-tombstoned schema keys, so the reconciliation test's two asserts hold by reading.

Tried to break it:

S1 (should-fix) — the two hints, and their zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES and console-overlay copies, never tell the person setting the gate that it applies to them too. The gate refuses ONE view and a dashboard "on every door and to an author as to anyone" (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:1668-1671`, `:1676-1678`; the code at `:1826-1829` and `:1850-1853`), and `liveness/view.json:180` records "a misspelled one now hides the view from everyone". The row this PR ships is a free-text tag box, so an administrator (or a dashboard builder in the in-page editor, which renders every section of `dashboardForm`) who types a capability they do not hold, or misspells one, publishes an item that no door serves them again: Studio cannot reopen it to clear the row. Recovery exists only outside the form (grant oneself that exact capability name in Setup, or a blind `PUT`). The hint lists who is refused as "anyone else", which a reader takes to exclude themself. The round-trip test does not reach this either: its author holds the capability. The fix is one sentence in each hint and its translations, to the effect of "this includes you: hold the capability yourself before you save, and a name nobody holds hides it from everyone"; the second PR's closed picker removes the misspelling but not the unheld pick, so the sentence stays true after it. If the seat prefers to carry it to the second PR instead, that is a deviation for the maintainer-facing record to name, not a silent drop.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):
- N1: the PR body's quick-read says a wrong capability name leaves the view "visible only to object editors" and that deleting the row's value restores it. On the tree that is the rule for an object's own `listViews` (ADR-0106 D4), not for a view item or a dashboard, which are refused to the author as well. PR-body prose; fixable without moving the head, and it should be, since it is the text the maintainer reads.
- N2: the dashboard hint's "Leave it empty and everyone sees this dashboard" is looser than the view hint's "everyone who can see the list": an ungated dashboard is still reached only through an app and navigation the person can open.
- N3: both hints say "pick one capability" over a control that, until the second PR, is typed, not picked.
- N4: `dashboard.zod.ts` still says, in the docblock above the key, "including why it says the gate is not enforced yet"; stale since #22639 and outside this diff, noted for a follow-up only.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1), open on this head.
